cards.text: Jesus enters the town of Jericho, and He's not stopping. He's just passing through. And there's a man in Jericho named Zacchaeus.

cards.question: Zacchaeus has a big title. What is he?

cards.text: Chief tax collector. VERY wealthy. And today, all that money can't buy him the one thing he wants: a look at who Jesus is.

cards.question: Zacchaeus can't see Jesus because Jesus has already gone by.

cards.text: Nope. There's a crowd, and Zacchaeus is small in stature. Friend, I'm a cookie stamper, I spent YEARS looking up at mixing bowls like they were mountains, so I FEEL this. So what does he do? He runs on ahead.

cards.question: Zacchaeus climbs a ___ tree to see Jesus.
Zacchaeus climbs that tree because Jesus is about to pass that way.

cards.text: Jesus comes to that spot, looks up, calls Zacchaeus by name and tells him to hurry down. Think about it, friend. You climb a tree just to get a LOOK, and the One everybody came to see looks STRAIGHT UP at YOU.

cards.question: Jesus tells Zacchaeus to hurry down out of the sycamore tree. What reason does Jesus give?

answers.text: He must stay at his house today
The crowd is about to block the road
He has a message for all of Jericho

cards.question: Zacchaeus hurries down from the tree and welcomes Jesus ___.
When the people see Jesus go to Zacchaeus's house, every one of them is happy about it.
All who saw Jesus go with Zacchaeus begin to grumble. What do they say?

answers.text: He has gone to be the guest of a sinful man
He has gone to stay with a wealthy man
He has passed by the rest of Jericho

cards.text: The whole crowd is grumbling. But Zacchaeus stands up and speaks to the Lord, and friend, everybody's about to hear this.

cards.question: What does Zacchaeus tell the Lord he gives to the poor?
Zacchaeus says that if he has cheated anyone, he will repay it ___.

cards.text: HALF of his stuff. FOUR times back. Friend, when I burn one cookie, I bake ONE more and call it even, and I'm PROUD of myself. Then Jesus answers him.

cards.question: Jesus tells Zacchaeus that today ___ has come to this house.
Jesus says salvation has come to Zacchaeus's house today. What reason does He give?

answers.text: This man too is a son of Abraham
This man has kept the whole law
This man was first to see Me

cards.text: Then Jesus says what the Son of Man came to do. Friend, I spent years lost in the back of a junk drawer, so lean in, because this line is the whole passage in one sentence.

cards.question: Jesus says the Son of Man came to ___ and to ___ the lost.

findings.problem: "He's not stopping" is something the text shows is wrong. Jesus stops in Jericho and stays at Zacchaeus's house (Luke 19:5-7). Luke 19:1 says only that He "was passing through."

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: "The one thing he wants" states Zacchaeus's feeling as fact and stretches the text. Luke 19:3 says only that he "was trying to see who Jesus was."

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The story card has five sentences ("Nope." / "There's a crowd..." / "Friend, I'm a cookie stamper..." / "So what does he do?" / "He runs on ahead.") and three beats: the crowd and his height, the joke, and running ahead.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Zacchaeus climbs that tree" points back to the tree from card 6, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences ("Jesus comes to that spot..." / "Think about it, friend." / "You climb a tree...").

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "He has gone to stay with a wealthy man" is true in the passage. Jesus does go to stay with Zacchaeus, who is "very wealthy" (Luke 19:2, 5). It is also close in meaning to the right answer ("guest" and "stay with," "a ... man"), so a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: Same wrong answer as above: it nearly matches the right answer.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: "Everybody's about to hear this" adds a fact. Luke 19:8 says Zacchaeus "said to the Lord." It never says everyone heard him.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences ("HALF of his stuff." / "FOUR times back." / "Friend, when I burn one cookie..." / "Then Jesus answers him.").

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 19 introduces "the Son of Man" without saying who He is. The text doesn't state here that Jesus is speaking of Himself.
findings.question: Should Papa Dorin say simply who the Son of Man is (Jesus, speaking of Himself), as the new-people rule asks? Or should he leave it open because Luke 19:10 doesn't say it, and let a dictionary pop-up cover it?
